GlossGenius Becomes Genius AI: Inside the $1.15B Bet on the Physical Economy
July 23, 2026
GlossGenius (Techstars 2015) has rebranded as Genius AI after raising a Series D at a $1.15B valuation, betting that AI will make human expertise more valuable, not less, in the in-person service economy.
GlossGenius (Techstars 2015) just changed its name. Not because the beauty and wellness scheduling app people fell in love with was broken, but because it had outgrown what its old name could hold.
This week, the company announced a Series D at a $1.15 billion valuation, pushing its total capital raised past $125 million. Alongside the raise, the company introduced a new corporate name, Genius AI, with GlossGenius continuing on as its flagship product.
The rebrand isn't cosmetic. As co-founders Danielle Cohen-Shohet and Leah Cohen-Shohet explained in a note published the same day, the customer base has grown well beyond beauty and wellness, and the product has grown well beyond software. The new name reflects both.
From Back-Office Tool to “Physical Economy” AI
GlossGenius launched on a simple premise. Let service professionals focus on their craft instead of their back office. The founders bootstrapped the company for years, deliberately starting with an industry they saw as one of the most technologically underserved in America, beauty and wellness. Every hour a stylist or esthetician spent chasing no-shows, reconciling payments, or managing a calendar was an hour taken from clients.
That focus has scaled. GlossGenius now says it powers more than 125,000 businesses across half of all U.S. ZIP codes, spanning salons, med spas, physical therapy practices, and wellness studios. The company estimates its platform has saved those businesses 112 million hours of administrative work and helped generate more than $2 billion in additional revenue, with the business itself approaching a $200 million revenue run rate this quarter.
The bigger claim in the founders' note is about where AI is headed next. Their argument is that as models automate more knowledge work, in-person, human expertise, think the stylist, the physical therapist, the trainer, becomes more valuable, not less. They point to roughly 8 million U.S. businesses built around this kind of hands-on service work, representing more than $2 trillion in annual spend. Genius AI's bet is that this "physical economy" is entering its best era, and that the winning platform will be the one that runs the admin work autonomously rather than just helping with it.
That shift is already visible in the product. Beyond its core scheduling, payments, and point-of-sale tools, GlossGenius has been rolling out AI agents, including a Growth Agent, a Marketing Agent, and a Reception tool that answers calls and texts around the clock, aimed at automating the busywork that surrounds every appointment rather than just recording it.
The Pitch, in One Line
The announcement's headline captures the thesis the company is now built around. "Your genius is the craft. Let everything else run itself." It's a bet that the value of human expertise rises as AI takes over everything adjacent to it, and that GlossGenius, now under the Genius AI banner, wants to be the layer that disappears so the practitioner doesn't have to think about it.
Learn more at genius.ai.

NEW YORK, NY / ACCESS Newswire / July 21, 2026 / Genius AI, the technology platform for in-person service businesses, today announced $44 million in Series D financing at a $1.15 billion valuation. The round was led by Lux Capital, with participation from Bessemer Venture Partners, Imaginary Ventures, L Catterton Growth, 2048 Ventures, StepStone Private Ventures, and other existing investors, bringing the company's total capital raised to more than $125 million. Source: Genius AI (EZ Newswire) Alongside the financing, the company announced its new corporate name, Genius AI. This name reflects the expansion of its customer base and product vision: helping every service business run itself. That work began with GlossGenius, which today is now one of the flagship products of Genius AI. GlossGenius automates workflows like scheduling, payments, marketing, staff, and client management. GlossGenius is used widely across single and multi-location businesses with staff in verticals like beauty, wellness, and health-related services. GlossGenius will be joined by additional agentic products that execute the work end-to-end rather than assist with it, as part of the Genius AI platform. In-person service businesses represent one of the largest opportunities for AI transformation. There are roughly 8 million of these businesses that generate more than $2 trillion in annual spend. Yet the average owner loses nearly a third of every week to administrative work. As advancing model capabilities make it possible to complete multi-step work autonomously, Genius AI believes AI will expand capacity for human-to-human care - making many services more human, not less. "The best work happens with a true partner beside you. As identical twins, we grew up with that - someone who understands you and makes you better. That's what we want for every owner," said Leah Cohen-Shohet, co-founder and Chief Business Officer of Genius AI. Today, more than 125,000 businesses across half of all U.S. ZIP codes run on the platform. The company estimates its products have saved customers 112 million hours of administrative work, helped them generate $2 billion in additional revenue, and facilitated more than 624 million client touchpoints. The company is approaching a $200 million revenue run-rate. "We believe technology in our space will do the opposite of what people fear: not flatten human craft into automation, but free people to be more present, more expressive, and more connected to the people they serve," said Danielle Cohen-Shohet, co-founder and CEO of Genius AI. "One of the most powerful things AI can do isn't to replace what makes us human. It is to give us room to be more human."

data.full_text:
At the Stripe Sessions SaaS Platform Leaders Summit, Stripe Head of Data and AI Emily Sands (left) discusses AI’s impact on commerce with Metropolis Cofounder and CEO Alex Israel and GlossGenius Founder and CEO Danielle Cohen-Shohet.

Last month, thousands of vertical SaaS leaders gathered at Stripe Sessions and Stripe’s inaugural SaaS Platform Leaders Summit to discuss what they’re seeing in the market and how vertical SaaS can stay differentiated as AI changes expectations for software.

Across the more than 16,000 platforms on Stripe—serving broad categories like home services and auto repair, as well as highly specialized verticals like tattoo parlors and funeral homes—many are looking to move beyond software by adding financial services like payments and lending. They’re working to embed themselves into operations in ways that are stickier and harder to displace than any feature set alone.

Here are five insights into how vertical SaaS platforms are building for the future.

1. AI is forcing platforms to expand beyond pure software

Concerns around AI commoditizing software businesses are real, but vertical SaaS platforms have an edge because they’re ingrained in the industries they serve. In a fireside chat with Stripe President John Collison, Toast President and CFO Elena Gomez advised vertical SaaS leaders to build closely around customer workflows in ways that pure software, and pure AI, can’t easily replicate: “The companies that win in vertical SaaS are the ones that stay deeply embedded in their customers’ worlds and never stop listening.”

One of the most effective ways vertical SaaS companies can integrate into customers’ day-to-day operations is by offering payments. As AI makes software features easier to replicate, payments can make a platform more integral to the financial workflows that run a business—processing transactions, tracking revenue, and managing cash flow.

Customers increasingly want this offering from platforms. Median payments adoption rose from 27% in 2024 to 40% in 2025. But adoption isn’t a solved problem: that still leaves a wide gap between the median platform and the top Stripe platforms, which achieve adoption rates of 80% or higher.

The platforms closing that gap make payments adoption a company-wide priority. “Starting with the ‘why’ is really important,” said Catherine Beley, VP of payments at GlossGenius. “Bring to the executive team that payments is the biggest revenue driver for the company, and then translate that into tangible goals—not just Gross Payment Volume, but ARR for the entire company.”

The platforms that reach the highest adoption rates then reinforce that strategy across product, go-to-market, and customer success. Phil Acree, VP of payments at Fullbay, a platform for commercial trucking repair shops, suggests baking payments into sales compensation plans: “Our software AEs are incentivized to bring up payments in their demos, and so are our onboarders and CSMs. There’s no customer interaction where someone on our team isn’t encouraging payments adoption.”

For platforms that succeed, Tidemark estimates that each customer who adopts embedded payments generates an average of $4,200 in incremental ARR for the platform.

Payments adoption impacts retention as well. According to 2026 Stripe data, platforms with embedded financial products see 11% lower annual churn, and those with a multiproduct strategy see 49% faster revenue growth than software-only peers.

“It’s very easy to talk about payments revenue in isolation,” said Ben Brideaux, SVP, financial services at Nextech. “A real opportunity for payments leaders is that second-order effect on other revenue within your business. If you can increase retention rate and net dollar retention, you start to see these compounding effects.”

2. Embedding more deeply into operations builds a stronger moat

Payments adoption at scale opens the door to additional products—and further stickiness. Commerce platform Shopify now offers embedded finance products like payments, capital, banking, and charge cards. Toast began as a restaurant point-of-sale system and added payroll, bill pay, and capital.

At Sessions, Obi Omile, CEO of theCut, a booking app for barbers, shared how Stripe Capital helped his own business grow—and how he quickly realized the thousands of barbers on his platform could benefit, too. Within 24 hours of sending out Capital offers, 167 barbers accepted $788,000 in financing.

“We knew there was demand, but we were really surprised by the speed of acceptance,” said Omile. “Barbers were accepting offers within three to four minutes of receiving the email.” Omile said Capital helped barbers buy new equipment, navigate seasonal slowdowns, and advertise their shops. “We continue to hear the same three things from our barbers: Capital helps them grow their business, build resilience, and expand.”

The moat doesn’t have to be strictly financial. Moxie embeds compliance tools into its platform so medspas don’t risk losing their licenses. Slice negotiates wholesale rates on pizza boxes for restaurants.

These are also the kinds of services that are difficult for a new AI-native competitor to offer from day one.

3. Vertical SaaS is finding success offering its own AI products

Stripe CRO Eileen O’Mara (left) with Byron Deeter of Bessemer Venture Partners and Tidemark’s Dave Yuan during a fireside chat at the SaaS Platform Leaders Summit at Sessions.

While building beyond software creates durable moats, platforms aren’t ceding the software layer either: 87% of SaaS platforms we surveyed say AI is more of an opportunity than a threat, and they’re moving quickly from experimentation to monetization.

Bessemer partner Byron Deeter pointed to Canva and Intercom as examples of non-AI-native platforms accelerating growth by adding agentic tools—Canva AI, a prompt-based design suite, and Fin, an AI customer service agent. “To me, the anxiety and fear around AI should be overshadowed by a ‘think of what we can do now’ mindset.”

Top vertical SaaS platforms are adapting. Toast IQ anticipates local food trends, so restaurants can plan menu changes or improve marketing. Quipli auto-generates leads for equipment rental dealers when new permits are filed. Clio’s AI assistant helps lawyers draft documents, summarize case files, and surface client insights.

Tidemark founder Dave Yuan framed it as simply meeting customer demand: “Your customers want agentic solutions from you. They want agents that help them do their jobs, that automate the drudgery work they don’t want to do.”

4. AI pricing is an active experiment

How to price and monetize those AI features is harder to pin down. Eighty-six percent of SaaS platforms with AI features are now charging for them, but 44% expect to make multiple pricing changes in the next 12 months as they work through the right model.

Some are bundling AI features into existing SaaS fees; others are breaking them out as stand-alone products through usage- or outcome-based pricing. Yuan’s advice: test before committing. “I see a lot of temptation to bundle in AI features, and that can make sense if you’re trying to get people to upgrade or use more of the product,” said Yuan. “But the biggest litmus test of whether you’re adding value is if your customers are paying for it, so platforms should consider charging for AI features in a premium tier or charging for them separately.”

5. Platforms are expected to lead the way on agentic commerce

Agentic commerce is changing how transactions happen, with AI agents taking a more active role in how purchases are discovered, decided, and completed. Platforms building that infrastructure today—from agent-readable catalogs to headless checkout APIs—are designing for the $5 trillion agentic opportunity.

For retail platforms, the challenge is more fundamental. “There’s a real challenge with the quality of retail data, and all of it has been optimized for human shopping channels and SEO,” said Dirk Hoerig, cofounder and managing director at commercetools. “The customer is now changing how they search. Instead of looking up ‘gray jeans,’ they’re typing, ‘I’m looking for an outfit I can wear for a speaking engagement—what do you recommend?’ That context is becoming far more relevant in agentic discovery.”

WooCommerce, Commerce, and commercetools are working to make their merchants’ catalogs discoverable and purchasable on popular LLMs, which requires rethinking how product data is structured.

What agentic commerce looks like varies by vertical. For Playtomic, it could be an agent booking a padel court reservation end to end. Metropolis wants to automate the parking transaction entirely: AI reads the license plate, charges the card, and opens the gate with zero human interaction. In legal and healthcare, agents might play more of a supporting role, handling scheduling, documentation, billing, and follow-up while human relationships remain the focus.

The common thread across verticals is that merchants are expecting platforms to be ready for whatever agentic commerce brings. “Nobody knows which agentic surfaces will win, so we’re not betting on one channel or one rail,” said Vova Tsukur, cohead of payments at Wix. “It’s the platform’s job to absorb that complexity so merchants don’t have to.”

Building what’s next

Stripe provides the infrastructure behind some of the most successful vertical SaaS platforms in the world—from Shopify to Mindbody to Substack.

At Sessions, we announced dozens of ways Stripe supports vertical SaaS, including a Platform growth studio to help capture more revenue and a path to embed Stripe Treasury and Stripe Issuing with just a few lines of code. Vertical SaaS platforms also have additional tools to help customers onboard faster, pay expenses with cards, dispute charges, access rolling lines of credit, and become agent-ready.

Check out the full list of Sessions announcements, and watch the keynotes and breakouts on demand. Plus, sign up for a Stripe Tour event near you to meet other vertical SaaS leaders in person.

Quick glossary as you read: backbar = professional-use supplies at the station; retail = products you sell to clients; POS= point of sale (checkout and payments); CRM = client records and notes; POs = purchase orders. Fresha has earned its reputation as one of the most popular booking platforms in the beauty and wellness industry. Its combination of free core software, built-in payment processing, and marketplace visibility has attracted over 130,000 businesses worldwide. For many salons, it’s a compelling first choice.

But as your business evolves, you might discover that Fresha’s approach doesn’t align perfectly with your specific needs. Perhaps the 20% commission on new marketplace clients is eating into your growth margins. Maybe you want deeper integration with your existing WordPress website. Or you might prefer a different balance between marketplace visibility and brand control.

That’s where this guide comes in. We’ll explore dedicated alternatives that excel in specific areas, whether you’re looking to:

Integrate booking directly into your WordPress website with full control over customization and branding

Leverage AI-powered automation and specialized enterprise tools for multi-location chains

Scale your growing team with transparent, predictable pricing and no marketplace commissions

Combine salon services with fitness classes in a platform built for multi-modality wellness

Present clients with a premium, beautifully designed booking experience

Start with a genuinely free booking solution backed by an established ecosystem

Access modern features like dynamic pricing and AI marketing tools at an affordable price

Some businesses might use these tools alongside Fresha for specific capabilities, while others might replace it entirely. This isn’t about finding a “better” platform; it’s about finding the right fit for your specific situation as your business grows. Let’s dive in.

What is Fresha?

Fresha is a cloud-based booking and business management platform designed for beauty and wellness businesses, including salons, barbershops, spas, and wellness centers. The platform has grown to serve over 130,000 businesses globally, positioning itself as an all-in-one solution that combines appointment scheduling with payment processing, marketing tools, and client management.

Its key features include:

Free core booking software for solo operators: The base platform costs nothing for individual professionals, with revenue generated through payment processing fees and marketplace commissions. Team plans may require subscriptions depending on your region.

Built-in payment processing: Integrated card payments with the option to require deposits or full prepayment

Marketplace visibility: Exposure to potential new clients searching for services in your area

Client management: Customer profiles, booking history, and automated reminders

Marketing tools: Basic email and SMS campaigns, promotions, and gift cards

Team management: Staff scheduling, commission tracking, and performance insights

Source: Fresha

Fresha’s appeal lies in its accessibility: businesses can get started without upfront software costs, and the marketplace provides a built-in client acquisition channel. The platform handles the technical complexity, allowing salon owners to focus on their craft.

However, Fresha’s model includes trade-offs that become more significant depending on your priorities. The 20% commission charged on new clients acquired through the marketplace can impact margins for businesses actively seeking growth through that channel. And for salons already invested in WordPress websites or preferring self-hosted solutions, Fresha’s standalone SaaS nature represents a different approach than native integration.

That’s why we’ve focused on alternatives that take different approaches in their areas of specialty.

How We Curated Our List of Fresha Alternatives

After researching Fresha and the broader salon software market, we identified that businesses often seek alternatives when they have specific preferences around:

Full control over their booking experience and branding: The ability to customize every aspect of how clients interact with their booking system, particularly through self-hosted solutions

Zero commission fees on client acquisition: Predictable costs that don’t scale with success in attracting new clients

AI-first enterprise automation: Advanced artificial intelligence features for call handling, marketing, and analytics

Deep integration with fitness verticals: Platforms built from the ground up for wellness businesses combining multiple service modalities

Premium visual design: A booking experience that matches high-end brand positioning

A genuinely free starting point: Robust features without monthly subscription costs

Modern features like AI marketing and dynamic pricing: Next-generation tools for independent professionals

Each platform on this list takes a distinct approach in one of these specific areas. Some readers might use these tools to complement Fresha, while others might replace it entirely based on their specific requirements.

❗DISCLAIMER: We aren’t covering every salon booking platform on the market. Our focus is on highlighting alternatives that take different approaches from Fresha’s model. The goal is to help you find tools that match your particular needs.

1. Salon Booking System — Best Alternative for WordPress Users Who Want Full Control and Zero Commissions

Salon Booking System is a comprehensive appointment scheduling plugin for WordPress designed specifically for service-based businesses including hair salons, barbershops, spas, and wellness centers. Created in 2016 by Dimitri Grassi, a WordPress web designer who believed the platform could handle more ambitious projects, it has grown steadily over nearly a decade in the market. The vendor reports nearly 10,000 premium installations, while WordPress.org shows over 3,000 active installations of the free version. This longevity, with many customers staying for 5-7+ years, demonstrates the kind of trust that comes from consistent development and responsive support.

Unlike cloud-based platforms like Fresha, Salon Booking System integrates directly into your existing WordPress website, giving you complete control over the booking experience, client data, and branding. Its key features include:

Native WordPress integration: Manage everything from your WordPress dashboard with seamless shortcode embedding

Multiple service and assistant booking: Unlike many booking plugins that limit customers to selecting one service per booking, clients can book multiple services and even multiple staff members in a single session which is ideal for appointments combining haircut, color, and treatment

Advanced booking rules: Multiple availability rules, resource-based booking, and sophisticated scheduling algorithms

Annual subscription pricing: Flat yearly fees with no per-booking or per-client charges

REST API access: Full developer capabilities for custom applications and integrations

40+ official add-ons : Extend functionality with Multi-Shops, WooCommerce checkout, Service Packages, and more

Staff mobile web app: Team members can manage their schedules from any device

Google Calendar sync : Two-way synchronization keeps all schedules aligned

Custom development services: Request specific features tailored to your business needs which is accessible even for smaller salons making a few hundred reservations per month

Source: Salon Booking System

For small to medium salons (typically 1-10 employees) that have built their online presence on WordPress and want to maintain complete ownership of their booking system, client relationships, and data, Salon Booking System provides a level of control and personalized support that larger platforms approach differently.

Why Choose Salon Booking System Over Fresha

Salon Booking System takes a fundamentally different approach from Fresha’s marketplace model, which may better suit certain business needs:

WordPress Integration: Your Booking System, Your Website, Your Brand

While Fresha operates as a separate platform that either directs clients away from your website or embeds as a widget, Salon Booking System becomes part of your WordPress site. The booking form lives on your pages, styled to match your design, with no third-party branding competing for attention.

Using simple shortcodes, you can display the booking form, staff calendars, service lists, or customer account areas anywhere on your site. The [salon/] shortcode creates the main booking page, [salon_booking_calendar] displays appointments organized by assistant, and [salon_booking_my_account] gives clients a personal dashboard for managing their bookings.

Source: Salon Booking System

This native integration means your SEO efforts, blog content, and booking system work together as a unified experience. Clients stay on your website throughout most of the booking process (though payment processing may involve external gateways depending on your configuration), maintaining the brand consistency that’s essential for premium positioning.

⚡ Salon Booking System in Action: A client discovers your salon through a blog post about hair care tips on your WordPress site. Interested, they click the “Book Now” button. Instead of being redirected to a third-party platform with different branding, they see a booking form that matches your website’s design exactly. They select a haircut, add a color treatment, and include a conditioning service which is an all in one booking. They choose their preferred stylist, pick a time slot, and complete the booking. Their information stays in your WordPress database, ready for you to nurture the relationship on your terms.

Annual Subscription Pricing: Pay for the Software, Keep Your Revenue

Fresha‘s 20% commission on marketplace-acquired new clients might seem reasonable initially, but the math changes as you grow. A salon booking £5,000 worth of services from marketplace-acquired clients would pay £1,000 in commissions to Fresha.

Salon Booking System operates on straightforward annual subscription pricing:

Basic Branded: €89/year for single-site use with all PRO features

Business: €139/year for two sites with 40+ add-ons and multi-location management

Agency Pass: €299/year for up to 10 sites with white-label options

Unlimited Pass: €499/year for unlimited installations

Every booking you receive, whether from existing clients or new ones who find you through Google, your marketing efforts, or word of mouth, belongs entirely to you. The flat annual fee means your costs remain predictable regardless of how many clients you serve.

⚡ Salon Booking System in Action: You invest in local SEO and social media marketing to attract new clients. A prospect finds your salon through Google, visits your website, and books a £200 color treatment. With Fresha’s marketplace, if that client had found you through their platform, you’d pay £40 in commission. With Salon Booking System, your €89/year subscription covers unlimited bookings from unlimited clients. The more successful your marketing becomes, the better your return on investment.

Deep Customization: Rules and Logic That Match Your Business

Salon Booking System offers three booking calculation modes (Basic, Advanced, and High End) that accommodate different operational complexities. The Advanced mode handles multiple services with varying durations, while High End mode considers execution order when multiple staff members perform services in a single booking session.

Source: Salon Booking System

The resource-based booking capability is particularly valuable for spas and medspas. You can define resources like “Massage Room 1,” “Laser Equipment,” or “Pedicure Station” with specific capacities. When a client books a service linked to a resource, the system performs a three-tiered availability check: first the resource, then the service, and finally the staff member.

Source: Salon Booking System

You can create:

Multiple availability rules for complex schedules (note: overlapping rules may require careful configuration to avoid conflicts)

Holiday rules for closures and special events

Booking offsets for buffer time between appointments

Assistant-specific rules that override general availability

This level of configurability means the booking system adapts to your operations, not the other way around.

A Partnership Approach: More Than Just a Plugin Provider

One aspect that sets Salon Booking System apart from larger WordPress booking plugins is its relationship-focused approach. With a smaller, dedicated customer base rather than tens of thousands of users, the team can offer something larger competitors cannot: genuine partnership.

This manifests in several practical ways. Support is highly responsive because you’re not just another ticket in a queue. Custom development services are accessible even for smaller salons making a few hundred reservations per month. If you need a specific feature that would benefit your business, you can request it directly, and if it’s valuable to the broader customer base, it often gets integrated into the core plugin.

Many features in the current version originated as custom solutions for specific client needs before being refined and released to everyone. This customer-driven development means the platform evolves based on real salon operations, not theoretical use cases.

Developer-Friendly Architecture: Build What You Need

For businesses with unique requirements or development resources, Salon Booking System’s REST API opens possibilities that closed platforms cannot offer. The API enables:

Retrieving and inspecting booking details programmatically

Searching for availability across services and staff

Creating, updating, and canceling bookings from external applications

Building custom mobile apps with your booking system as the backend

Source: Swagger Hub

The Zapier integration extends connectivity to thousands of applications, enabling automated workflows like creating a Google Meet session for each new booking.

⚡ Salon Booking System in Action: Your salon group wants a custom-branded mobile app that connects to your booking system. Using the REST API, your developer builds an iOS and Android app that pulls real-time availability, allows clients to book appointments, and sends push notifications for reminders. With the white-label options available on Agency and Unlimited plans, your app can display your branding exclusively, depending on your implementation.

Data Ownership: Your Clients, Your Database

With Salon Booking System, core client and booking data lives in your WordPress database on your hosting server. You maintain significant control over this information, from how it’s stored to how it’s used for marketing.

The system includes data export capabilities for reservations (CSV format) and integrates with standard WordPress tools for user data management. It’s worth noting that certain features like SMS notifications, payment gateways, and integrations like Zapier may transmit some data to external services, so review your specific configuration for complete data flow understanding.

True Multi-Location Architecture

Zenoti was specifically designed for chain operations. A single dashboard provides unified oversight of all locations with centralized guest profiles, cross-location booking capabilities, and consolidated reporting. Transparent, Predictable Pricing

Fresha’s 20% commission on marketplace-acquired new clients can become costly as you grow. Vagaro charges a straightforward £20/month base fee for a single calendar, with £10 added for each additional team member (up to seven, after which additional calendars are free). Comprehensive All-in-One Features

Vagaro includes inventory management with automated low-stock alerts, employee management with tiered commission structures, payroll processing (via add-on), email marketing with 1,000 free emails monthly, Daily Deals promotions, and the MySite website builder.
